name: Kåkern Bridge
facts: The Kåkern Bridge, a 303‑metre cantilever road bridge, opened in 2002, linking the islands of Flakstadøya and Moskenesøya across the Kåkernsundet strait in Norway’s Lofoten archipelago.
Before 2002, the original Kåkern Bridge was a 228‑metre suspension span that served traffic from 1961 until the new cantilever structure was completed just south of it.
As one of several Lofoten bridges, the Kåkern Bridge’s 303‑metre length makes it a key maritime link, while the Fredvang Bridges remain the only other crossing between Flakstadøya and Moskenesøya.
